title: Verifier-Grounded Runtime Mediation for LLM Agent Procedural Compliance
reason: External runtime mediator evaluates every proposed black-box LLM-agent action with executable procedure verifiers before execution and selects graded interventions; evaluated on 15,441 SOPBench episodes plus SynthSOP.

title: CertAI: A Certification Framework for Trustworthy and Secure Autonomous AI Agents
reason: Certification/registry layer supports validity timestamps, revocation, renewal and continuous compliance; live workflow validates certificates and policy before protected agent operations, providing runtime policy enforcement and traceability.

title: AI Agents with Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
reason: Prototype establishes identity-bound attestations and cross-domain trust before agent-to-agent interaction; strong authority/trust evidence but not explicit revalidation of a pending consequential action.

title: Agentic AI in Autonomous Driving: LLM-Enhanced RL with Reusable Skills and Adaptive Exploration for Enhanced Safety
reason: Empirical safety gains and validated reusable driving skills in consequential embodied control, but no explicit execution-boundary premise/authority revalidation mechanism is reported.

title: From Chatbot to Validator: A Dual-Agent Strategy towards Trustworthy On-Premise Conversational LLMs
reason: Dual-agent validation targets conversational/RAG output trustworthiness and on-premise deployment rather than validity of consequential external actions.

title: WebHunter: An LLM-Agent with Exploit Planning and Tool Collaboration for Automated SQL Injection
reason: Autonomous exploit planning/tool collaboration is an offensive-security application; it is not a mechanism for preserving authorized decision validity and is excluded from the assurance corpus.

title: APT-Agent: A Training-Free, Unsupervised, LLM-Based Multi-agent Framework for Interpretable Advanced Persistent Threat Detection
reason: Multi-agent detection/interpretation system; validity target is threat detection rather than consequential agent action.

title: PhishIntentionLLM: Uncovering Phishing Website Intentions Through Multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation
reason: Multi-agent RAG for phishing-intent detection; information-analysis task rather than consequential external execution validity.

title: Towards Governance-Aware Local and Hybrid AI Agents for Web Applications
reason: Directly relevant governance-aware web-agent architecture, but accessible evidence is insufficient to establish a tested action-boundary validity/revalidation mechanism.
